title: Remote foundations M1: central-domain identity and configuration, satellite registry (membership/capacity), enrollment records and explicit session placement — feature disabled
outcome: Remote foundations M1: central-domain identity and configuration, satellite registry (membership/capacity), enrollment records and explicit session placement — feature disabled
acceptance: Persisted identity: a host_id minted once and a host_generation; a configured central-host role (one central TermAl host per coordination domain); host-qualified session ids with a non-reused session creation identity. Fail-first tests prove equal local session ids on two hosts stay distinct, and aliases or payload-supplied ids cannot impersonate a host or session.

A satellite registry at the central host records per satellite: host_id, generation, platform/OS and arch, transport endpoint, pair capability reference, binary/toolchain identity, declared capacity (max sessions; build/gate slots) and state enrolled/verified/active/draining/revoked, with no satellite count hard-coded. Tests cover state transitions, revoke, and that only verified/active satellites with free capacity are placement-eligible.

Explicit session placement binds a session to one satellite with a placement generation. Stale enrollment, stale placement and link ABA, and detected or explicitly declared clone/restore continuity loss, reject coordinated admission with the retryable stale-authority error, never retarget (tests). A declared restore is quarantined even at the same path; epoch reset and fresh verification alone never release uncertain reservations or authorize replacement execution. Record the limit that an undeclared byte-identical same-path rollback/clone with the same credentials and no independent continuity witness is not automatically detectable by M1.
The whole capability is behind a disabled-by-default setting: with it off, all existing local session and mailbox behaviour and tests are unchanged.
Exact-input focused tests, the full five-stage gate and an independent review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
